chunks: My father (rah) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to us from Salamah ibn al-Khattab from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi from Ali ibn Ya'la from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Hamran from his father from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever performs ablution and wipes (the parts of the body), a good deed is recorded for him; and whoever performs ablution and does not wipe until his ablution dries, thirty good deeds are recorded for him.
ai.seo_question: What is the reward difference between wiping and not wiping after ablution?
ai.summary: In *Thawab al-A'mal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to highlight the spiritual merit of the Sunnah practice of *tamandul* (wiping the face and hands after washing). The hadith establishes a comparative reward structure, granting thirty good deeds for allowing the water to dry naturally versus only one for wiping, thereby emphasizing the virtue of patience and adherence to the Prophet's customary manner of completing ablution.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. My father (rah) said: it was narrated to us by Sa’d b. Abdillah from Salamah b. al-Khattab from Ibrahim b. Muhammad al-Thaqafi from Ali b. Ya’la from Ibrahim b. Muhammad b. Hamran from his father from Abi Abdillah (a.s.) who said: “
A person who wipes the parts of body after ablution will get a single reward and the person who does not wipe will get thirty rewards.”
